target.title: fix(qqbot): add actionable setup error guidance
target.body:
## Summary

Add shared, account-aware QQBot setup guidance to credential, token, API, and network failures.

Fixes #65868.

## What Problem This Solves

QQBot failures previously left users with terse or raw errors. The first version of this PR made those errors actionable, but always named `QQBOT_APP_ID` and `QQBOT_CLIENT_SECRET`. Those environment variables resolve only for the default account, so that advice could not repair a named account.

## Why This Change Was Made

QQBot config resolution intentionally distinguishes the default account from named accounts:

- default: `channels.qqbot.appId` plus `clientSecret`/`clientSecretFile`, with `QQBOT_APP_ID` and `QQBOT_CLIENT_SECRET` fallback;
- named: `channels.qqbot.accounts.<id>.appId` plus `clientSecret`/`clientSecretFile`, without environment fallback.

The setup helper now accepts account context for missing-credential paths. Context-free token/API failures use account-neutral guidance rather than suggesting default-only environment variables.

## User Impact

- Default-account startup and outbound failures show both supported config and environment recovery paths.
- Named-account failures show the exact account-scoped config path and do not mention ignored `QQBOT_*` variables.
- Token, structured API, and network failures retain the docs link and actionable account-neutral credential guidance.

## Changes

- Make missing-credential guidance account-aware.
- Pass `account.accountId` from gateway, text outbound, and media outbound paths.
- Make token/API/network guidance account-neutral.
- Add focused regression tests for default, named, and context-free guidance.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

Executed the production helper through Node/tsx after the fix (synthetic account IDs; no credentials):

```text
named-account runtime output:
QQBot not configured (missing appId or clientSecret). Set channels.qqbot.accounts.operations.appId and clientSecret (or clientSecretFile), then see https://docs.openclaw.ai/channels/qqbot
default-account runtime output:
QQBot not configured (missing appId or clientSecret). Set channels.qqbot.appId and clientSecret (or clientSecretFile), or set QQBOT_APP_ID and QQBOT_CLIENT_SECRET, then see https://docs.openclaw.ai/channels/qqbot
```

This demonstrates that named-account runtime output no longer advertises the default-only environment variables.

### Validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/qqbot/src/engine/config/setup-guidance.test.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/api/token.test.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/api/api-client.test.ts` — passed (3 files, 14 tests).
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check <six changed QQBot files>` — passed.
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json <six changed QQBot files>` — passed (0 warnings, 0 errors).
- `git diff HEAD^ --check` — passed.
- `gitleaks git --no-banner --redact --log-opts='HEAD^..HEAD' --exit-code 1` — passed, no leaks found.
- Patch-file `gitleaks dir --redact` scan before commit — passed, no leaks found.

### Typecheck note

A direct local `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p extensions/qqbot/tsconfig.json --noEmit` was attempted but is not valid in this linked worktree: the reused dependency tree cannot resolve the checkout's `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*` workspace exports, producing broad pre-existing module-resolution failures. Focused tests and targeted lint cover the changed surface; hosted CI remains authoritative for the full extension type lane.
